purpose: The Engineering Assurance release this repository adopts, and the artifacts it actually reads from that release. Component version pins are NOT restated here: the packaged compatibility matrix is their authority and a second copy would drift from it.
matrix_authority: compatibility-matrix.json embedded in the pinned engineering-assurance CLI. scripts/check_shared_pins.py observes the local toolchain and delegates every verdict to the native engineering-assurance compatibility command.
registry: Every npm component resolves from the public npm registry (registry.npmjs.org). The internal npm.ix mirror must not appear in any requirement, pin, lockfile, or .npmrc, and is not an oracle for whether a release landed. Querying an @agent-ix package needs --@agent-ix:registry=https://registry.npmjs.org; a bare --registry does not override the scoped .npmrc entry.

engineering_assurance.release_form: planned git tag v0.3.2, a source distribution; this candidate migration is not merged until the accepted tag exists

repinned_workflow_component.why: The hosted workflow formerly pinned @agent-ix/quoin@0.22.5, which the packaged compatibility matrix names explicitly incompatible: it predates the quoin change-assurance surface. An earlier migration moved to 0.23.1; the Stage 1 EA 0.3.2 matrix now requires the published 0.24.1. ix-flow@0.0.4 was absent from the old workflow and is now installed at 0.2.3.

repinned_ix_flow.why: TL-192: the packaged compatibility matrix authoritative for this repository's pin (matrix_authority above) classified ix-flow strictly at the exact pinned version, so a locally-installed 0.2.3 against a v0.2.0 matrix pinning 0.0.4 classified as unknown, not compatible, and failed the local qualification gate. engineering-assurance v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, agent-ix/engineering-assurance#47) re-pins the matrix to ix-flow 0.2.3 with human acceptance recorded (accepted_by Peter Krenesky, accepted_at 2026-09-10, after the local TC-107 gate passed against public ix-flow 0.2.3). At TL-192, this repository's engineering_assurance pin moved from v0.2.0 to v0.2.1 so the workflow literal and the matrix authority agreed; the then-current quire-cli and quoin versions were unchanged by that historical bump.

stage1_ea_adoption: This candidate moves the active assurance lane to the reviewed Engineering Assurance 0.3.2 matrix, Quire CLI 0.33.0 (engine 0.47.1), and Quoin 0.24.1 while retaining ix-flow 0.2.3. The matrix is the only compatibility authority. The V1 campaign AP-002/MP-007 records the source-bound eleven-milestone release measurement; Quoin 0.24.1 has no independent measurement-verdict checker, so AP-002 recommends rather than requires checker promotion, while the executable campaign gate still requires eleven passes. This migration is not a release claim until the matrix has named human acceptance and v0.3.2 is tagged.
consumed_artifacts_note: The pinned native CLI embeds and classifies the compatibility matrix. This repository consumes its structured result through the CLI protocol and reads no separate file from an EA Python distribution. The tagged CLI and its named matrix acceptance are the authority. Historical digest-consumer reductions remain recorded in change-assurance.json.

upstream_dependency.why: The compiled pin is the exact Stage 1 tl-syntax 0.4.0 candidate revision. Its MIT-licensed unbounded formula owner and shared corpora supply the evaluator contracts. Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock, fuzz/Cargo.lock, src/lib.rs, and this record agree on the revision; the previous 9de638d revision is retained in the superseded list.

known_drift: Resolved by the TL-192 bump to v0.2.1: engineering-assurance v0.2.0 packaged compatibility-matrix.json with accepted.state = pending_human_acceptance and shipped no human_acceptance_recorded predicate (agent-ix/engineering-assurance#20). v0.2.1 (release: accept ix-flow 0.2.3 matrix, #47) carries accepted.state = accepted with accepted_by and accepted_at populated, so the historical v0.2.1 record carried that acceptance rather than a branch head.

Historical: the human acceptance itself was never in doubt: Peter Krenesky accepted the FR-012 matrix on 2026-09-01, attributed on engineering-assurance main as ae50e13, and the historical v0.2.1 release carried it (see above).

Quire resolves the spec-artifacts-process module from the machine's installed Filament modules, and nothing in this repository pins that module's revision. At that historical review, the installed default counted the 8 suite-registry rows and reported 118 counted, 116 backed: 65 requirement criteria, 45 test-matrix rows, and six of eight suite rows. SUITE-001 and SUITE-002 are deliberately non-runnable and their absence is asserted independently. Recorded under agent-ix/tl-mltl#47 rather than pinned, because the packaged compatibility matrix carries no module-revision entry to classify against.
